Proto-Germanic *wegaz Proto-West Germanic *weg Old English weġ Middle English wey English way From Middle English way, wey, from Old English weġ, from Proto-West Germanic *weg, from Proto-Germanic *wegaz, from Proto-Indo-European *weǵʰ-. senses.d: A road, a direction, a (physical or conceptual) path from one place to another.
ex: Do you know the way to the airport?  Come this way and I'll show you a shortcut.
We lied our way through the debriefing.

senses.d: A means to enter or leave a place.
ex: We got into the cinema through the back way.
If you're ever 'round this way, come over and visit me.
It's a long way from here.
Twenty miles surely is a long way to walk.

senses.d: A method or manner of doing something; a mannerism.
ex: He's finally seen the error of his ways.
You're going about it the wrong way.  He's known for his quirky ways.  I don't like the way she looks at me.

senses.d: A set of values and customs associated with and seen as central to the identity of a group of people.

ex: He's in a bad way.
When I returned home, I found my house and belongings in a most terrible way.

senses.d: Possibility (usually in the phrases ‘any way’ and ‘no way’).
ex: There's no way I'm going to clean up after you.

senses.d: Determined course; resolved mode of action or conduct.
ex: My little sister always whines until she gets her way.

senses.d: A tradition within the modern pagan faith of Heathenry, dedication to a specific deity or craft, Way of wyrd, Way of runes, Way of Thor etc.
ex: To walk the Way of the Runes, you must experience the runes as they manifest both in the part of Midgard that lies outside yourself and the worlds within. (Diana Paxson)

senses.d: Yes; it is true; it is possible.
ex:
- We searched the vehicle. It was clean, so we did the body cavity searches.
- No way.
- Way!
We repeated this ritual of “no way - way, no way - way” over the years.
on a time as they together way'd, / He made him open chalenge[…].
I used to live way over there.
The farmhouse is way down the bottom of the hill.

senses.d: Much, far, by a great degree.
ex: I'm a way better singer than Emma.
I'm way too tired to do that.
I'm way tired.
String theory is way cool, except for the math.
Sitting in the way back of the bus
some day in the way future me and @HowdyDuda are gonna have to come for a visit…
